decisions.reason: The smooth branch computes g_t from losses without requiring that vector to be measurable. On Omega={a,b} with trivial sigma-algebra and its probability measure, let A={a}, K=[0,1], d=1, T=2, D=G=1, x_1=1, f_1(omega,x)=1_A(omega)x on R and f_2=0. Every realized loss is differentiable convex and every gradient has norm at most 1, but x_2=1-1_A is not measurable: its inverse image of {0} is A. Continuity of projection cannot supply missing input measurability. The repair explicitly requires measurable computed gradients as well as supplied vectors.
